items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: He said, “Well I think Ben Webster is available.”

ctx.x: It came out, anyhow, I thought it came out good. I listened to those tapes recently, they sound pretty good. But it was very trying to read that kind of stuff. And some guys just read that right off. I’m not a world class reader. I can read, particularly if I get a little peek at it ahead of time I’m okay, but I’m not a studio style sight reader. There were some trying moments with John, we had a misunderstanding about whether I was supposed to play or not at a Dizzy concert and I wound up playing and he told me,…

that was — but anyhow Helen and I started rehearsing and about this time I didn’t know Orrin Keepnews that well. But, and he’s not that accessible a person until you get to know him. He’s not a “hail fellow well met” like — he’s very much an individual and he can have a dour, but he’s a great, great man but he’s not somebody going to slap you on the back say how you doing you know. So we ran into each other, our sons went to the same school. So Father’s Day I ran into him up there. We got to talking and he was…
